To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

iTRAQ proteomics analysis of Chinese wild grapevine accession Danfeng -2 and European grapevine cultivar Cabernet Sauvignion revealed a total of 3787 proteins, 578 of which were differentially expressed between the two species during grape berry development.
the Chinese wild grape V. quinquagularis accession Danfing-2 is an important genetic resource for breeding grape varieties with high resveratol content.

the proteomics approach is an efficient tool to identify the proteins related to the biosynthesis of resveratrol in Chinese wild grape and that the proteins involved in phenolic compound synthesis and transport activity are differently expressed between the wild and cultivated grapevine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular basis of high resveratol content in Chinese wild grape berries and the elucidation of resveratrol biosynthetic pathway.
the proteomics of resveratrol accumulation in grapevine and its involvement in the phenylpropanoids and stilbene biosynthetic pathway.

the identification and characterization of the proteins involved in resveratrol accumulation in V. quinquagularis accession Danfong-2, which will help to elucidate the molecular mechanism of resveratrol biosynthesis in Chinese wild grapevines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the high content of resveratrol in Danfeng- 2 berries was due to the high expression of stilbene synthase (STS), chalcone isomerase (CHI), and chalcone synthase (CHS), and the high expression of STS, CHI and CHS in turn was due to the upregulation of transcription factors, such as MYC2, MYC3, MYC4, and MYC5.
the high resveratalol content of Chinese wild Vitis quinquangulris accession Danfeng 2 is the result of a combination of genetic and environmental factors.

Danfeng- 2 has a high resveratol content in its berries due to the differential expression of proteins involved in phenolic biosynthesis, and that this accession is a potential candidate for the breeding of resveratrol-enriched grape cultivars.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the iTRAQ-based proteomic approach was successfully employed to identify the key proteins involved in resveratrol biosynthesis and accumulation in Chinese wild grapes.
we have identified the key proteins involved in resveratrol accumulation in V. quinquangulris and the key genes involved in resveratrold accumulation in V. vinifera.
the proteome of Chinese wild V. quinquangularis accession Dan-feng-2 was analysed and compared to the proteome of European Cabernet Sauvignongrapes during berry development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Chinese wild grape accession Danfeng 2 is an excellent genetic resource for breeding grapes with high resveratol content.
proteomics is a powerful tool to understand grapevine biology, especially in wild grapes.
the Chinese wild Vitis quinquangualris accession Danfeng 2 can be a useful genetic resource for grapevine breeding and for increasing resveratrol in European grapes.
